_comment: R0 SEED disclosure-target registry per ADR-2605302130 §2 — WORLDWIDE (multi-jurisdiction) coverage. Each entry is the coded 窓口 / 住所 / メールアドレス / portal / 手続き / fee / deadline so himotoki can route + file procedurally. Now spans the major DSAR (own-data-only) and public-records/FOIA channels across blocs: JP, US (federal + CA/NY/TX), EU (GDPR/EU instruments + DE/FR), UK+Commonwealth (UK/CA/AU/IN/SG), and INTL-ROW (BR/MX/KR), in addition to the original major data-controller DSAR targets. ALL entries ship verificationStatus=unverified-seed: per G14, NO live dispatch may occur against an unverified entry — these MUST be human/Council-verified (and re-checked within the freshness window) before himotoki_dispatch will transmit. Specific portalUrl / contactEmail / postalAddress / feeJpy / statutoryDeadlineDays below are best-effort public references and are EXPECTED to drift; treat them as routing scaffolds for wayfinding only, never live use, not authoritative contacts.

targets.organization: US Federal FOIA — agency records request (foia.gov consolidated portal)
targets.authority: The specific federal executive-branch agency holding the records (each agency runs its own FOIA office); cross-agency portal operated by DOJ Office of Information Policy / OMB
targets.legalBasis: Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552 (as amended, incl. FOIA Improvement Act of 2016)
targets.notes: Federal Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) records request. PUBLIC-RECORDS / FOIA channel, NOT a personal-data right — any person may request records about an agency's activities; nine exemptions + three exclusions apply (5 U.S.C. § 552(b),(c)). FOIA covers federal EXECUTIVE-branch agencies only — Congress, federal courts, and the President's immediate staff are excluded. For records about YOURSELF held by an agency, pair with the Privacy Act (us-privacy-act-access). foia.gov routes to the holding agency's FOIA office; each agency has its own FOIA regulations, fee schedule, and intake form — re-verify the holding agency before filing. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing/wayfinding only, never live use.

targets.organization: US Privacy Act — access to / amendment of your own federal records
targets.postalAddress: Agency-specific Privacy Act office, located via the agency's published System of Records Notices (SORNs) in the Federal Register; many agencies accept Privacy Act requests through the same office as FOIA (see https://www.foia.gov)
targets.authority: The federal agency that maintains the relevant System of Records (each agency's Privacy Act / FOIA office)
targets.legalBasis: Privacy Act of 1974, 5 U.S.C. § 552a (right of access § 552a(d)(1); amendment § 552a(d)(2))
targets.notes: Privacy Act request for access to / amendment of your own federal records. OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound: a US citizen or lawful permanent resident may access and seek correction of records about THEMSELVES held in a federal 'system of records' (retrieved by name/SSN/identifier). Distinct from FOIA — requesters commonly file under BOTH 5 U.S.C. § 552 and § 552a to maximize disclosure. Exemptions apply (e.g., law-enforcement systems under § 552a(j),(k)). Requires identity verification. SORNs and per-agency intake addresses change; confirm the current SORN before filing. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: US — California CCPA/CPRA consumer Right to Know / access + deletion (to the business)
targets.authority: The covered business (data controller) itself is the request recipient; enforcement/oversight by the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) and California Attorney General
targets.legalBasis: California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 as amended by the CPRA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100 et seq. (right to know § 1798.110 / § 1798.115; right to delete § 1798.105; right to correct § 1798.106)
targets.notes: California CCPA/CPRA consumer 'Right to Know' / access + deletion request. OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound DSAR against private businesses (not government). The request goes to the BUSINESS via its own designated CCPA method (typically a 'Do Not Sell/Share My Personal Information' link, privacy-request web form, or toll-free number), NOT the regulator — CPPA/AG handle complaints and enforcement, not individual fulfillment. Business must confirm receipt within ~10 business days and respond within 45 days (extendable to 90). CPPA oversight: https://cppa.ca.gov . Each business sets its own intake URL/form; CPPA regulations are actively evolving (clarifying regs effective 2026). Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: US — California Public Records Act request (CPRA, Cal. Gov. Code § 7920)
targets.authority: The California state or local government agency that holds the records
targets.legalBasis: California Public Records Act, Cal. Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq. (recodified 2023; formerly Gov. Code § 6250 et seq.); access right rooted in Cal. Const. art. I, § 3(b)
targets.notes: California public records request. PUBLIC-RECORDS / FOIA-equivalent for California GOVERNMENT bodies (not private companies — for businesses use the CCPA entry). ACRONYM COLLISION: 'CPRA' here is the California PUBLIC RECORDS Act, NOT the California Privacy Rights Act. Recodified to Gov. Code § 7920 et seq. effective Jan. 1, 2023; older sources still cite § 6250 et seq. Agency must respond within 10 days (extendable). Per-agency intake URLs vary widely and change; confirm the holding agency's current channel. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use. Confidence medium: statute recodification verified from general knowledge; exact current provenance PDF URL not re-fetched this session.

targets.organization: US — New York Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) records request
targets.authority: The New York State or local government agency holding the records (each agency designates a Records Access Officer, RAO); advisory oversight by the NY Committee on Open Government
targets.legalBasis: New York Freedom of Information Law, N.Y. Public Officers Law, Article 6, §§ 84-90
targets.notes: New York Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) records request. PUBLIC-RECORDS / FOIA-equivalent for New York STATE and LOCAL government bodies (not private companies). Each agency designates a Records Access Officer; agency must acknowledge within 5 business days and provide records or a date certain. Appeals go to the agency's designated FOIL appeals officer, then Article 78 proceeding. Guidance via NY Committee on Open Government (advisory only, does not adjudicate). Per-agency RAO contacts and the central portal URL change; confirm the holding agency's current RAO before filing. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use. Confidence medium: statute cite (POL Art. 6 §§84-90) is well-established; exact current portal URL not re-fetched this session.

targets.organization: US — Texas Public Information Act (PIA / Open Records) request
targets.postalAddress: The governmental body's public-information officer (written request). AG oversight + cost/complaint help: Texas Attorney General Open Records Hotline 512-478-6736 / 1-877-673-6839; AG e-filing for rulings: https://apps.portal.texas.gov/OAGPIAeFiling/
targets.authority: The Texas governmental body holding the records (each designates a public-information officer); the Texas Attorney General Open Records Division rules on withholding and charges
targets.legalBasis: Texas Public Information Act, Texas Government Code, Chapter 552 (§ 552.001 et seq.)
targets.notes: Texas Public Information Act (PIA / Open Records) request. PUBLIC-RECORDS / FOIA-equivalent for Texas GOVERNMENT bodies (not private companies). All government information is presumed public; the officer may NOT ask why you want it. Body must 'promptly' release non-confidential info; if it cannot within 10 business days it must give a date certain, and to withhold it must seek an AG ruling. The AG e-filing portal is for the BODY's ruling requests and overcharge complaints, not the requester's initial request. Confirm the holding body's current public-information officer. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: EU — GDPR Right of Access (Subject Access Request) to any data controller
targets.contactEmail: (controller's published privacy@/dpo@ address — no central portal; submit in writing to the controller's DPO/privacy contact)
targets.authority: The individual data controller (any company/organization processing your personal data); the firm's Data Protection Officer (DPO) is the entry point. Supervisory authority for complaints = the relevant national DPA (e.g. CNIL in FR, BfDI/Länder DPAs in DE).
targets.legalBasis: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Article 15 (right of access by the data subject); response due within one month per Art. 12(3); copy free of charge per Art. 15(3)/12(5).
targets.notes: GDPR Right of Access (Subject Access Request) to any data controller, EU-wide. No mandatory form — submit in writing (email or postal letter) directly to the controller's DPO/privacy contact, identifying yourself and requesting a copy of all personal data and the Art. 15(1) information. GDPR is directly applicable in all 27 member states but the controller's contact address varies per organization — there is NO central submission portal. Controller may request proof of identity (Art. 12(6)) where reasonable doubt exists. Member-state derogations (e.g. German BDSG §34, trade-secret/third-party limits) can narrow what is disclosed. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED for routing/wayfinding — never live use.

targets.organization: EU — Public access to EU institution documents (Request a Commission document)
targets.authority: European Commission Secretariat-General (Transparency unit); parallel registers exist for the European Parliament and Council of the EU.
targets.legalBasis: Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 regarding public access to European Parliament, Council and Commission documents; grounded in Art. 15(3) TFEU. Reply within 15 working days, extendable once by 15 working days.
targets.notes: Public access to EU institution documents ('Request a Commission document'). PUBLIC-RECORDS (FOIA-equivalent) channel, not a personal-data request — open to any EU citizen/resident/business. Official route is the Commission's request form (requires an EU Login account); written requests in any official EU language are also accepted. AsktheEU.org (https://www.asktheeu.org) is an NGO-run helper (Access Info Europe), NOT the institution itself — confirm the official Commission portal URL and EU Login requirement before any real use; the Regulation is under active revision (legislative train), so deadlines/scope may change. Consultation on-site and copies under 20 A4 pages are free. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED for routing/wayfinding — never live use.

targets.organization: EU — Germany Federal Freedom of Information request (IFG)
targets.authority: The individual federal public body holding the information; the BfDI (Bundesbeauftragte für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit) acts as ombudsperson/oversight, not the document holder.
targets.legalBasis: Informationsfreiheitsgesetz (IFG) of 5 September 2005, in force 1 January 2006 — establishes an unconditional right of access to official information of federal agencies (no need to show legal interest).
targets.notes: Germany Federal Freedom of Information request (Antrag nach dem Informationsfreiheitsgesetz / IFG). PUBLIC-RECORDS (FOIA) channel — open to any person regardless of nationality/domicile. Submit to the relevant federal authority in writing, electronically (email), or even verbally; no specific form required. FragDenStaat (the linked portal) is an NGO (Open Knowledge Foundation Deutschland) helper, not an official portal — its responses are public by design, so do NOT use it for anything containing your own private data. IFG covers FEDERAL bodies only — each Bundesland has its own (or no) transparency law. Fees may apply for substantial requests. BfDI info: https://www.bfdi.bund.de . Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED for routing/wayfinding — never live use.

targets.organization: EU — Germany GDPR/BDSG Right of Access to a controller (Art. 15 DSGVO / §34 BDSG)
targets.contactEmail: (controller's privacy/DPO contact — written request by email/letter; no national portal)
targets.authority: The data controller's DPO; oversight/complaints to the competent supervisory authority — BfDI for federal bodies and telecoms, or the relevant Land DPA (one of 16 state authorities) for private-sector controllers.
targets.legalBasis: Art. 15 GDPR (right of access) as applied in Germany, with national modulation by Bundesdatenschutzgesetz (BDSG) §34 (limits where info must by law/nature be kept secret, incl. business/trade secrets and overriding third-party interests).
targets.notes: Germany GDPR/BDSG Right of Access to a controller (Auskunftsersuchen nach Art. 15 DSGVO / §34 BDSG). OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound — you may request only YOUR personal data. Written request (email/letter) to the controller's privacy contact; if ignored, file a complaint with the competent Land DPA or BfDI. §34 BDSG can lawfully narrow the response (trade secrets, third-party rights); the BGH has confirmed the scope is broad (incl. internal notes/correspondence) — case law evolves. There is no single national submission portal; the correct Land DPA depends on the controller's seat. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED for routing/wayfinding — never live use.

targets.organization: EU — France GDPR Right of Access to a controller (droit d'accès RGPD), CNIL fallback
targets.contactEmail: (controller's DPO/privacy contact; CNIL complaint if unanswered: https://www.cnil.fr/fr/plaintes)
targets.authority: The data controller's DPO (délégué à la protection des données); CNIL (Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés) is the supervisory authority for complaints, not the first-line responder.
targets.legalBasis: Art. 15 GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) as implemented by the Loi n° 78-17 du 6 janvier 1978 relative à l'informatique, aux fichiers et aux libertés (Loi Informatique et Libertés, as amended).
targets.notes: France GDPR Right of Access to a controller (droit d'accès RGPD), with CNIL complaint fallback. OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound. Request directly to the controller (email, web form, on-line account, or postal letter — no prescribed form). If unanswered within one month, lodge a complaint (plainte) with CNIL. CNIL does not itself supply your data — it supervises and can act on complaints; first send the request to the controller. The controller may ask for an ID copy only in case of reasonable doubt about identity. One-month response deadline per GDPR Art. 12(3). Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED for routing/wayfinding — never live use.

targets.organization: EU — France access to administrative documents (CADA, accès aux documents administratifs)
targets.authority: The administration holding the document (first instance); the CADA (Commission d'accès aux documents administratifs) is the mandatory pre-litigation review body if access is refused.
targets.legalBasis: Originally the Loi n° 78-753 du 17 juillet 1978; now codified in the Code des relations entre le public et l'administration (CRPA), Livre III (articles L300-1 et seq.) on the right to obtain communication of administrative documents.
targets.notes: France access to administrative documents (accès aux documents administratifs / saisine de la CADA). PUBLIC-RECORDS (FOIA) channel — broad right for any person; free of charge. First request the document directly from the holding administration (letter/email; no form). If refused (or implicit refusal after 1 month silence), seise the CADA within 2 months (online form, letter, or email). Citizen guide: https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F2467 . The 1978 law is now recodified into the CRPA — cite the CRPA articles for current text. Seising CADA is a MANDATORY prerequisite before any administrative-court litigation, and the 2-month deadline is strict. Documents with third-party personal data or covered secrecy may be redacted or withheld. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED for routing/wayfinding — never live use.

targets.organization: UK — Subject Access Request / Right of Access (SAR), ICO complaint fallback
targets.authority: Data controller directly (any organisation holding your personal data); Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) is the supervisory authority / complaint body
targets.legalBasis: UK GDPR Article 15 (right of access), as supplemented by the Data Protection Act 2018 (DPA 2018), ss. 45 & 94 for law-enforcement/intelligence processing
targets.notes: UK Subject Access Request / Right of Access (SAR). OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound (controller may verify ID), one free copy, normally answered within 1 calendar month. Submit directly to the controller (verbally or in writing, including by email or social media); ICO is the regulator/complaint route. The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 amended parts of UK GDPR / DPA 2018 in 2025 — re-confirm response-time and 'stop-the-clock' clarification rules before relying. Third-party requests require proof of authority. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for wayfinding, never live use.

targets.organization: UK — Freedom of Information request (FOI) to a public authority
targets.authority: The UK public authority that holds the information (department, council, NHS body, etc.); ICO is the regulator/appeal body
targets.legalBasis: Freedom of Information Act 2000 (for England, Wales, Northern Ireland); Freedom of Information (Scotland) Act 2002 for Scottish public authorities (regulated by the Scottish Information Commissioner)
targets.notes: UK Freedom of Information request (FOI). PUBLIC-RECORDS only (not personal data of others — that routes to a SAR). Written request (email/letter/online form) to the public authority, with name + contact details; ~20 working days to respond; exemptions apply. Scotland uses a separate Act (FOI(S)A 2002) and separate regulator (Scottish Information Commissioner) — pick the right statute for the body's jurisdiction. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: Canada — ATIP (Access to Information / Privacy Act) federal request
targets.authority: The federal government institution holding the records; Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat operates the online intake; Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC) is the oversight body
targets.legalBasis: Privacy Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. P-21) for one's own personal information; Access to Information Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. A-1) for general government records
targets.notes: Canada Personal Information / Access to Information Request (ATIP). Privacy Act path is own-data-only, identity-bound; Access to Information Act path is public-records (ATIA general-record requests have historically required the requester be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or present in Canada — Privacy Act personal-info requests are open to all). 30 calendar-day statutory response. Covers FEDERAL institutions only — provinces (e.g. Ontario FIPPA/MFIPPA, BC FIPPA, Quebec) have their own laws and channels. ATIP Online or by mail/form to the institution's ATIP coordinator. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: Australia — Access to Personal Information (APP 12) request
targets.authority: The APP entity (private organisation or Australian Government agency) holding the personal information; Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) is the regulator/complaint body
targets.legalBasis: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Schedule 1, Australian Privacy Principle 12 (APP 12 — Access to personal information); for agencies, the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Cth) may also apply to personal records
targets.notes: Australia Access to Personal Information Request (APP 12). OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound, no required form or stated reason. Request made directly to the entity (phone, email, letter or e-record). Ten refusal grounds exist (e.g. serious threat to safety, impact on others' privacy, commercially sensitive evaluative info). For records held by a Commonwealth agency, access is often handled under the FOI Act 1982 instead of/in parallel with APP 12. State public-sector bodies sit under separate state privacy laws. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: Australia — Freedom of Information request (federal, FOI Act 1982)
targets.authority: The Australian Government agency or minister holding the documents; OAIC handles Information Commissioner reviews
targets.legalBasis: Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Cth)
targets.notes: Australia Freedom of Information Request — federal (FOI Act 1982). PUBLIC/GOVERNMENT documents. Written request to the agency stating it is made under the FOI Act (most agencies publish an FOI page/form); agency acknowledges within 14 days and decides within 30 days; no application fee, and no charge where documents contain only your own personal information; ten exemption categories apply. Covers FEDERAL agencies only — each Australian state/territory has its own FOI/RTI act and regulator. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: India — Right to Information request (RTI Online, Central Government)
targets.authority: Public Information Officer (PIO) of the relevant Central Government public authority; Central Information Commission (CIC) is the appellate/oversight body
targets.legalBasis: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Act No. 22 of 2005)
targets.notes: India Right to Information Request (RTI application). PUBLIC-RECORDS access for any Indian citizen; small statutory fee; PIO to respond generally within 30 days. SCOPE LIMIT: rtionline.gov.in is for Central Government public authorities only — State Government bodies (incl. Govt of NCT Delhi) must use their own state RTI portals/offices or the application is returned without refund. India also has a separate personal-data regime (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023) with its own access rights once its rules are in force — RTI is NOT the personal-data DSAR channel. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: Singapore — PDPA Access & Correction request to an organisation
targets.authority: The organisation holding the personal data (private sector); Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) is the regulator/complaint body
targets.legalBasis: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA) — Access and Correction Obligation, Part 5 / sections 21–22 and the Personal Data Protection Regulations
targets.notes: Singapore Access Request for Personal Data (PDPA Access & Correction Obligation). OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound. Request made directly to the organisation (typically to its Data Protection Officer); organisation must provide the data plus information on how it was used/disclosed in the prior year, and may charge a reasonable fee. SCOPE: PDPA governs PRIVATE-sector organisations — Singapore public agencies are covered separately by the Public Sector (Governance) Act and not by the PDPA access right. Confirm current fee/timeline guidance with PDPC before any reliance. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing only, never live use.

targets.organization: Brazil — LGPD data-subject access request to a controller / DPO
targets.contactEmail: (controller's DPO/encarregado contact, published per LGPD Art. 41 in its privacy notice; ANPD oversight: https://www.gov.br/anpd/pt-br)
targets.authority: Data controller (controlador) via its appointed DPO (encarregado); supervised by ANPD (Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados)
targets.legalBasis: Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD), Lei nº 13.709/2018, Art. 18 (esp. Art. 18, II — direito de acesso) and Art. 19 (form/timing of confirmation and access; simplified reply immediate, full declaration within 15 days)
targets.notes: Brazil LGPD data-subject access request (Requisição de acesso do titular — direito de acesso). OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound. There is no single national DSAR portal — the request goes to each individual controller's DPO, whose contact must be published per Art. 41; route via the controller's privacy notice. ANPD is the supervisor/complaint body, not a relay for the original access request. ANPD regulations and response-time guidance evolve; confirm the controller's current DPO contact before filing. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing/wayfinding only — never live use.

targets.legalBasis: Lei de Acesso à Informação (LAI), Lei nº 12.527/2011, regulated by Decreto nº 7.724/2012; response within 20 business days, extendable by 10
targets.notes: Brazil Access to Information (FOIA) request via Fala.BR (Pedido de Acesso à Informação — LAI, Plataforma Fala.BR — Módulo LAI). PUBLIC-RECORDS (FOIA) channel, not a personal-data DSAR. Fala.BR covers federal executive bodies plus thousands of opted-in states/municipalities/entities; some sub-national bodies run their own portals. Account/CPF (or equivalent) typically required to file. CGU periodically updates Fala.BR scope and UI. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). targets.organization: Mexico — ARCO rights request to a private controller (LFPDPPP)
targets.contactEmail: (private controller's data-protection contact, per its aviso de privacidad; federal oversight post-INAI: https://www.gob.mx/buengobierno)
targets.authority: Data controller (responsable) via its designated privacy officer / departamento de datos personales; oversight transferred to the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno (post-INAI dissolution)
targets.legalBasis: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares (LFPDPPP), published/replaced 20–21 March 2025; ARCO rights (Acceso/Rectificación/Cancelación/Oposición) exercised against the responsable
targets.notes: Mexico ARCO rights request to a private controller (Solicitud de derechos ARCO — Acceso, Rectificación, Cancelación, Oposición). OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound. MAJOR DRIFT: INAI was dissolved (constitutional reform pub. 20 Dec 2024) and a NEW LFPDPPP took effect 21 Mar 2025, transferring authority to the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno; secondary regulations and the new oversight body's request channels were still settling as of 2026 — verify the current authority and any official portal before filing. ARCO requests go to the private controller first; the authority is the complaint/escalation route. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing/wayfinding only — never live use. Confidence medium: post-INAI reorganization still settling.

targets.organization: Mexico — public information / public-sector ARCO via Plataforma Nacional de Transparencia (PNT / SISAI 2.0)
targets.authority: Sujetos obligados (public bodies) via the Plataforma Nacional de Transparencia (SISAI 2.0); guarantor functions reorganized post-INAI under the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno + state guarantor bodies
targets.legalBasis: Ley General de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (LGTAIP); for public-sector personal data, Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de Sujetos Obligados (LGPDPPSO) — ARCO/ARCOP against public bodies
targets.notes: Mexico access to public information / public-sector personal-data request via Plataforma Nacional de Transparencia (Solicitud de acceso a la información / ARCO ante sujetos obligados — PNT / SISAI 2.0). Dual purpose: public-records (FOIA) AND personal-data (ARCO) requests against PUBLIC bodies. SISAI 2.0 replaced INFOMEX in Sept 2021 (INFOMEX now consultation-only). The post-INAI institutional reorganization migrated obligated subjects to new federal guarantor functions; portal governance was in transition through 2025–2026 — verify the current operator/authority. Private-sector controllers use the ARCO entry (LFPDPPP), not the PNT. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing/wayfinding only — never live use. Confidence medium: post-INAI portal governance in transition.

targets.organization: South Korea — PIPA right-of-access request to a personal-data handler
targets.authority: Personal-information handler (개인정보처리자) directly; supervised by the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC, 개인정보보호위원회)
targets.legalBasis: Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA / 개인정보 보호법), Article 35 (right to access / 열람); related rights Art. 36 (correction/deletion), Art. 37 (suspension of processing); data portability added effective Mar 2025
targets.notes: South Korea PIPA right-of-access request to a personal-data handler (개인정보 열람 요구). OWN-DATA-ONLY, identity-bound. The access request is made to the individual handler; for public-institution holdings access may be requested via the privacy portal (privacy.go.kr). The PIPC handles disputes/complaints and the privacy.go.kr portal supports certain public-institution access and dispute-mediation flows rather than acting as a universal relay. Access may be limited where prohibited by other law or where it would harm a third party (Art. 35(4)). PIPA was substantially amended (2023, effective 2024–2025); confirm current article numbering and the handler's channel before filing. PIPC: https://www.pipc.go.kr . Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA). Transparent, non-pretextual, rate-limited, lawful-channel-only. No legal advice. UNVERIFIED SEED scaffold for routing/wayfinding only — never live use.

targets.organization: South Korea — Official information-disclosure (FOIA) request via open.go.kr
targets.authority: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (행정안전부) operates open.go.kr; each public institution processes its own requests
targets.legalBasis: Official Information Disclosure Act / Act on the Disclosure of Information by Public Institutions (공공기관의 정보공개에 관한 법률); decision within 10 days, extendable by 10
targets.notes: South Korea official information-disclosure (FOIA) request via the Information Disclosure Portal (정보공개 청구 — open.go.kr). PUBLIC-RECORDS (FOIA) channel, not a personal-data access right. Requests may also be filed in person/by mail/fax to the holding institution; certain categories (incl. third-party private information) are exempt from disclosure. Portal scope and disclosure-exemption interpretation evolve; verify the current institution and exemptions before filing. Consent-gated, identity-bound, own-data-only (DSAR) or public-records (FOIA).
